annotation.title_clean: How a non-conscious robot could be an agent with capacity for morally responsible behaviour
annotation.title_en: How a non-conscious robot could be an agent with capacity for morally responsible behaviour
annotation.summary_en: Philosophical journal article arguing that non-conscious robots can be moral agents with a substantial degree of free will and responsibility, using an event-causal libertarian theory of free will and Vargas's revisionist theory of responsibility. It is a conceptual contribution to robot moral agency, not a governance instrument.
key_provisions_or_claims: Defends an internalist (standardist) view in which robots can hold moral responsibility without phenomenal consciousness.
Builds on event-causal libertarianism and a revisionist account of responsibility, both of which come in degrees.
Argues that advanced non-conscious robots can have a stronger form of free will and responsibility than is commonly defended.
Positions itself between compatibilist and libertarian views, and between standardists and functionalists.
